correctness.rationale: Direct Gaussian-overlap derivation confirms the photon-number generating function, and differentiating factorial moments yields exactly \(\Pi_m=G^{(m)}(-1)/G^{(m)}(1)\). The Taylor expansion at -1 proves the exact parity sign and critical cancellation. The denominator has a unique dominant square-root branch; the numerator has two distinct branch points whose local Darboux expansions are uniformly valid across the critical equality of their moduli. Exact analytic prefactor simplifications yield \(\Pi_m=(-1)^mR_-^{m+1/2}+R_+^{m+1/2}+O(\max(R_-,R_+)^{m+1/2}/m)\). A derivative of their logarithmic ratio establishes the claimed fixed-s crossover. Pure-state and threshold boundaries are separated correctly. Direct truncated Fock-space reproduction and high-precision coefficient checks corroborate but are not the proof.

value.rationale: Multiple-photon subtraction is a motivated optical preparation and Wigner-origin parity a direct witness, but an all-m sign criterion alone would be only an algebraic use of known formulas. The meaningful additional fact is the explicit exponentially small contrast, sharp unit prefactors, and thermal offset scale \(1/m\) with a universal even/odd hyperbolic profile. This clarifies the sensitivity of high-order parity contrast to thermal contamination at the exact known thermal threshold, without claiming any finite-sample advantage or general Wigner-negativity volume.
